# iliad-136 — new renderings (21.400–501)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| νηπύτιε / νηπύτι’ (vocative, 21.410, 21.441, 21.474; a scolding address between gods) | "Childish one" | "You child" | "fool", "babe", "infant", "silly one"; adapts the Odyssey’s νηπύτιος "like a babe" / "like children" (13.292, 20.200) to a vocative, and keeps the three occurrences the same |
| ἡ κυνάμυια (Hera of Aphrodite, 21.421) | "the dog-fly" | "that dog-fly" | "that bitch", "shameless fly"; follows κυνάμυια "dog-fly" in iliad-135 (21.394), where Ares says it of Athena |
| ἀρείων (ὅσσον ἀρείων εὔχομ’ ἐγὼν ἔμεναι, 21.410) | "how much better" | "how much better" | "braver" (kept for ἀρείων of a man’s courage, 2.707), "stronger" (κρείσσων), "mightier" (φέρτερος); the comparison is general, as in the Odyssey’s ἄρειον "better" |
| εὔχομ’ ἐγὼν ἔμεναι (21.410–411) | "I declare myself to be" | "I declare myself to be" | "boast", "pray"; εὔχομαι "declare" as in the table’s ἱκέτης δέ τοι εὔχομαι εἶναι |
| ἰσοφαρίζεις / ἀντιφερίζεις (ὅτι μοι μένος …, 21.411, 21.488) | "to me in might you compare yourself" · "against me in might you set yourself" | "you match yourself with me in might" · "you set yourself against me in might" | "match yourself" in `l`, "rival", "vie with"; follows the table’s ἰσοφαρίζει (`l` "compares himself", `i` "matches"); the two verbs are kept apart |
| οὕτω κεν τῆς μητρὸς ἐρινύας ἐξαποτίνοις (21.412) | "Thus might you pay off in full your mother’s Erinyes" | "So you would be paying in full for your mother’s Erinyes" | "the Furies", "atone for your mother’s curses", "pay for your mother’s anger" (each resolves the Erinyes); follows the Odyssey’s μητρὸς Ἐρινύες "a mother’s Erinyes" (11.280) |
| τρέπεν ὄσσε φαεινώ (21.415) | "back she turned her two eyes, shining" | "turned her shining eyes away" | "bright eyes", "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις); φαεινός keeps "shining" (6.19); ὄσσε πάλιν "eyes away" as at 3.427 |
| πυκνὰ μάλα στενάχοντα (21.417) | "groaning very thickly" | "groaning again and again" | "groaning heavily" (βαρὺ στενάχων, 1.364), "groaning deeply", "thick and fast" |
| μόγις δ’ ἐσαγείρετο θυμόν (21.417) | "hardly was he gathering in his spirit" | "with difficulty he was drawing his spirit together" | "recovered his breath", "came to himself" (each decides what θυμός is); ἀγείρω "gather" as at 2.438 |
| οὖρον ἀρούρης (21.405; οὖρος "boundary-mark", Ionic for ὅρος) | "a boundary of the plough-land" | "a boundary of the plough-land" | "boundary-stone" (the stone is the thing set, not the word), "landmark"; ἄρουρα keeps "plough-land" |
| ἑπτὰ … πέλεθρα (21.407) | "seven plethra" | "seven plethra" | "seven acres", "seven hundred feet" (the unit is not certain); the note says it is a length of about a hundred feet |
| ἐκόνισε δὲ χαίτας (21.407) | "he made his hair dusty" | "soiled his hair with dust" | "defiled", "stained his locks"; κόνις "dust" kept |
| τεύχεά τ’ ἀμφαράβησε (21.408) | "his armour clanged about him" | "his armour clanged about him" | "rang", "rattled", "crashed" (reserved for κτυπέω); ἀραβέω "clang" |
| ἐπευχομένη ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (21.409, of Athena) | "and over him, vaunting, winged words she spoke:" | "and in triumph over him spoke winged words:" | "praying", "boasting" alone; follows the table’s ἐπευχόμενος "vaunting" / "in triumph" (21.121) and ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα |
| αὐτίκ’ Ἀθηναίην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (21.419, feminine of a shared line) | "at once to Athena winged words she spoke:" | "she at once spoke winged words to Athena:" | shipped masculine in iliad-021 ("At once to Athena winged words he spoke:"); only the gender of the subject changes |
| καὶ δ’ αὖθ’ (21.421) | "and indeed again" | "and see" … "that dog-fly is leading" | "and lo", "behold", "once more"; the particle of surprised complaint, with αὖθε "again" |
| ἐπιεισαμένη (21.424) | "rushing upon her" | "springing upon her" | "attacking", "lunging"; aorist participle of the verb of swift motion, not ἐπιείσομαι "go against" |
| τὼ μὲν ἄρ’ ἄμφω κεῖντο … ἣ δ’ ἄρ’ ἐπευχομένη (21.426–427) | "The two, then, both lay on the much-nourishing earth, / and she, vaunting, winged words spoke:" | "Both of them lay on the earth that feeds so many, and she, in triumph over them, spoke winged words:" | follows χθονὶ πουλυβοτείρῃ "the much-nourishing earth" (8.73) and the table’s ἐπευχομένη |
| τοιοῦτοι … ὡς Ἀφροδίτη ἦλθεν Ἄρῃ ἐπίκουρος ἐμῷ μένει ἀντιόωσα (21.428–431) | "Such now may all be … as Aphrodite / came, an ally to Ares, meeting my might" | "Would that all … were like this now … to meet my might" | "reinforcement", "helper" (ἐπίκουρος is "ally" in iliad-008, -015, and ἀρωγός "helper"); ἀντιόωσα "meeting" as ἀντιάω in iliad-134 (21.151) |
| θωρηκτῇσιν (Ἀργείοισι, 21.429) | "corseleted" | "corseleted" | "armoured", "mailed", "breastplated"; follows πύκα θωρηκτάων "closely corseleted" (12.317) |
| θαρσαλέοι καὶ τλήμονες (21.430) | "bold and enduring" | "bold and enduring" | "daring", "stout-hearted"; θαρσαλέος "bold" (5.601), τλήμων "enduring" (Odyssey 5.670) |
| ἄμμες (21.432) | "we" | "we" | "we two", "we gods"; the Aeolic form of ἡμεῖς, a plural that includes all the gods |
| αὐτὰρ Ἀπόλλωνα προσέφη κρείων ἐνοσίχθων (21.435, whole line) | "But to Apollo addressed the lord earth-shaker:" | "And the lord earth-shaker said to Apollo:" | "the mighty earth-shaker", "Poseidon" in `l`; follows the table’s κρείων ἐνοσίχθων "the lord earth-shaker" (5.282) |
| Φοῖβε τί ἢ δὴ νῶϊ διέσταμεν; (21.436) | "Phoebus, why then do we two stand apart?" | "Phoebus, why do we two stand apart?" | "hold aloof", "have we drawn apart", "stand off"; the dual νῶϊ "we two" kept |
| ἀμαχητί (21.437) | "without a fight" | "without a fight" | "unfought", "without battle", "without a struggle" |
| χαλκοβατὲς δῶ (21.438) | "the bronze-floored house" | "the house with the bronze floor" | follows the table’s χαλκοβατὲς δῶ (8.321); the note repeats that floor or threshold is disputed |
| γενεῆφι νεώτερος (21.439) | "younger in birth" | "the younger by birth" | "junior", "younger in years"; -φι is the instrumental ending, as in κρατερῆφι βίηφιν |
| ἄνοον κραδίην (21.441) | "senseless … heart" | "senseless heart" | "foolish", "mindless", "witless" (ἄνοος is ἀ- + νόος "mind"); κραδίη "heart" |
| ἀγήνορι Λαομέδοντι (21.443) | "manly Laomedon" | "proud Laomedon" | "noble", "lordly", "arrogant"; follows the table’s ἀγήνωρ ("manly" in `l`, "proud" in `i`, 4.548) |
| θητεύσαμεν εἰς ἐνιαυτὸν μισθῷ ἔπι ῥητῷ (21.444–445) | "we worked for hire for a year / for an agreed wage" | "worked for hire for a year, for an agreed wage" | "served as hired hands", "laboured", "for a fixed hire"; ῥητός "agreed, spoken"; ἐνιαυτός "year" (11.248) |
| ὃ δὲ σημαίνων ἐπέτελλεν (21.445) | "and he, giving orders, laid his charges." | "and he gave the orders and laid his charges on us." | "directing", "commanding" (reserved for κελεύω); follows the table’s σημαίνω "give orders" and ἐπιτέλλω "lay a charge" |
| ἵν’ ἄρρηκτος πόλις εἴη (21.447) | "that unbreakable the city might be" | "so that the city might be unbreakable" | "indestructible", "impregnable"; follows ἄρρηκτος "unbreakable" (2.489) |
| εἰλίποδας ἕλικας βοῦς βουκολέεσκες (21.448) | "the rolling-gaited, crumple-horned cattle were wont to herd" | "used to herd the cattle of rolling gait and crumpled horn" | "kept", "tended"; the -εσκ- iterative shown as "were wont to" / "used to"; the cattle as in the table’s εἰλίποδας ἕλικας βοῦς |
| πολυπτύχου … ὑληέσσης (Ἴδης, 21.449) | "many-folded, wooded" | "many-folded, wooded" | "many-ridged", "forested"; follows πολυπτύχου Οὐλύμποιο "many-folded" (8.411) and ὑλήεις "wooded" |
| κνημοῖσι (Ἴδης ἐν κνημοῖσι, 21.449) | "in the spurs of Ida" | "in the spurs of … Ida" | "glens", "slopes", "foothills" (each picks a sense); κνημός a spur or shoulder of a mountain |
| πολυγηθέες ὧραι (21.450) | "the much-gladdening seasons" | "the seasons, bringers of much gladness" | "joyous", "pleasant", "bounteous"; πολυ- + γηθέω "rejoice" |
| βιήσατο μισθὸν ἅπαντα (21.451) | "he used force upon us two, as to the wage, all of it" | "used force on us two and kept back all our wage" | "robbed us of", "defrauded", "forced from us"; the note gives the double accusative |
| Λαομέδων ἔκπαγλος (21.452) | "Laomedon, terrifying" | "terrifying Laomedon" | "terrible", "fearsome"; follows ἔκπαγλος "terrifying" (10.448, 1.146) |
| πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὕπερθε δήσειν (21.453–454; sense of ὕπερθε unclear) | "feet and hands, above, to bind" | "to bind our feet and hands together, above" | "hand and foot", "tightly", "behind his back" (each decides what ὕπερθε means); the note says it is unclear |
| περάαν νήσων ἔπι τηλεδαπάων (21.454) | "to carry across to far-off islands" | "to carry us across to far-off islands" | "sell into slavery" (the sale is a sense, not the word), "ship", "banish"; τηλεδαπός "far-off" |
| στεῦτο … ἀπολεψέμεν οὔατα χαλκῷ (21.455) | "he declared … to strip off the ears … with bronze" | "he claimed that he would strip off the ears" | "swore", "vowed" (turned down in the table for στεῦτο), "cut off", "lop off"; ἀπολέπω "strip off"; στεῦτο `l` "declared", `i` "claimed", as the table’s row (2.597) |
| κεκοτηότι θυμῷ (21.456) | "with a resentful heart" | "with resentful hearts" | "angry", "bitter", "with a grudge"; κότος "resentment" (Odyssey table) |
| οὔτησε κατ’ αἰγίδα (21.400) · τῇ μιν … οὔτησε (21.402; οὐτάω of a thrust that lands on the aegis and wounds no one) | "thrust at the aegis" · "There at her … thrust" | "stabbed at the aegis" · "stabbed at her" | "wounded" (the table’s οὐτάω; here nothing is wounded, so it would be false); the same departure as οὔτησε κατ’ ἀσπίδα (11.434) |
| πρόχνυ κακῶς (21.460) | "forward on the knee, evilly" | "utterly and in evil plight" | "miserably" (reserved for δειλός), "wretchedly" (reserved for δύστηνος), "on their knees"; the note gives πρό + γόνυ |
| τοῦ δὴ νῦν λαοῖσι φέρεις χάριν (21.458) | "On his account, then, now to his people you bring favour" | "it is on his account that you now bring favour to his people" | "you do him a favour", "serve him", "show gratitude"; the construction is loose and the note says so |
| σαόφρονα (21.462) | "sound-minded" | "sound-minded" | "prudent", "sensible", "wise" (reserved for πεπνυμένος); σάος "sound" + φρήν |
| ζαφλεγέες τελέθουσιν (21.465) | "are very-blazing" | "blaze with life" | "flourish", "burn bright", "are in full bloom" (each decides what blazing means); ζα- "very" + φλέγω |
| παυώμεσθα μάχης (21.467) | "let us cease from battle" | "let us quickly cease from battle" | "stop the fight", "give over", "withdraw" |
| οἳ δ’ αὐτοὶ δηριαάσθων (21.467) | "and let those men themselves fight on" | "and let them go on fighting by themselves" | "contend", "struggle", "wrangle"; follows the table’s δηριάασθαι "go on fighting" (16.96) |
| αἴδετο … πατροκασιγνήτοιο μιγήμεναι ἐν παλάμῃσι (21.468–469) | "he was ashamed to be mingled in the hands of his father’s brother" | "ashamed to meet his father’s brother hand to hand" | "uncle", "to fight"; πατροκασίγνητος "father’s brother" kept |
| πότνια θηρῶν Ἄρτεμις ἀγροτέρη (21.470–471) | "the lady of wild beasts, Artemis of the wild" | "the lady of wild beasts, Artemis of the wild" | "mistress of the beasts", "queen of the wild"; "lady" for πότνια (Odyssey table: πότνια νύμφη "the lady nymph"); ἀγροτέρη "of the wild", agreeing with "wild goats" (17.295) |
| ὀνείδειον φάτο μῦθον (21.471) / ὀνειδείοις ἐπέεσσι (21.480) | "a reproachful word she spoke" / "with reproachful words" | "spoke a reproachful word" / "with reproachful words" | "taunting", "abusive", "insulting"; one rendering for ὀνείδειος at both places |
| μέλεον δέ οἱ εὖχος ἔδωκας (21.473) | "an idle boast to him you have given" | "given him an idle triumph" | "a wretched boast" (μέλεος "idle" 10.480, "wretched" avoided), "hollow", "empty" (ἀνεμώλιος); εὖχος "boast" / "triumph" as in the table |
| ἐπέτρεψας (νίκην Ποσειδάωνι, 21.473) | "entrusted" | "entrusted" | "yielded", "handed over", "surrendered"; the table’s ἐπιτρέπω "entrusted" with an object |
| ἔχεις ἀνεμώλιον αὔτως (21.474) | "an empty thing, just so" | "an empty thing, to no purpose" | "for no reason" and "idly" (the table keeps these for other contexts), "in vain" (reserved for ἄλλως), "without more ado" (does not fit); αὔτως `l` "just so", `i` "to no purpose", as the table’s row (2.342) |
| ἄντα Ποσειδάωνος ἐναντίβιον πολεμίζειν (21.477) | "opposite Poseidon head-on to fight" | "that you will fight Poseidon head-on" | "face to face" (the table keeps it for ἀντίον ηὔδα and turns it down for ἐναντίβιον), "in open might", "man to man"; ἐναντίβιον "head-on" as in the table (8.255, 10.451) |
| Διὸς αἰδοίη παράκοιτις (21.479) | "the revered consort of Zeus" | "Zeus’ revered wife" | "his queen", "noble wife"; αἰδοίη "revered" (Odyssey table), παράκοιτις "consort" / "wife" (4.228) |
| κύον ἀδεές (21.481) | "dog, fearless one" | "you dog, you fearless one" | "shameless" (kept for ἀναιδής), "bold", "reckless"; follows the Iliad’s own shipped row (iliad-050, 8.423: "dog, fearless one" / "you fearless one"); the shipped Odyssey (odyssey-092, 19.91) has "unafraid dog", a different book’s wording that the Iliad row does not follow |
| τοξοφόρος (τοξοφόρῳ περ ἐούσῃ, 21.483) | "bow-bearing" | "bow-bearer" | "archer", "armed with the bow"; φέρω "bear" |
| σὲ λέοντα γυναιξὶ Ζεὺς θῆκεν (21.483–484) | "a lion to women Zeus made you" | "Zeus made you a lion to women" | "against women", "a lioness among women"; the note gives the old belief about Artemis |
| κρείσσοσιν ἶφι μάχεσθαι (21.486) | "with the stronger ones with force to fight" | "to fight powerfully against those who are stronger" | "mightier" (reserved for φέρτερος); κρείσσων "stronger" (16.688); ἶφι as in the table’s ἶφι μάχεσθαι |
| ὅσσον φερτέρη εἴμ’ (21.488) | "how much stronger I am" | "how much stronger I am" | "mightier", "better" (ἀμείνων); the table’s φέρτερος "stronger" (2.201, 6.158, 21.264); κρείσσων is "stronger" too (21.486, same passage), the table’s own overlap |
| ἔμαρπτε … αἴνυτο τόξα … ἔθεινε (21.489–491) | "seized … took the bow … she beat" | "seized … took the bow … beat" | "grasped", "snatched"; τόξα, the plural, kept as "the bow" with a note |
| ἐντροπαλιζομένην (21.492) | "her, turning back again and again" | "as she kept turning back again and again" | follows the table’s ἐντροπαλιζομένη "turning back again and again" (6.496) |
| δακρυόεσσα δ’ ὕπαιθα θεὰ φύγεν (21.493) | "And tearful, away from under, the goddess fled" | "Tearful, the goddess fled away" | "weeping", "in tears" in `l`; ὕπαιθα "from under, away" |
| ὥς τε πέλεια, ἥ ῥά θ’ ὑπ’ ἴρηκος … χηραμόν (21.493–495) | "like a dove which from under a hawk flew into a hollow rock, a cleft" | "like a dove which flew from a hawk into a hollow rock, into a cleft" | "pigeon" (πέλεια "dove" as the table’s πέλειαι), "falcon", "hole", "crevice"; ἴρηξ "hawk", χηραμός "cleft" |
| οὐδ’ ἄρα τῇ γε ἁλώμεναι αἴσιμον ἦεν (21.495) | "nor was it fated for her to be caught" | "for it was not her fate to be caught" | "doomed", "destined"; follows αἴσιμον "fated" (8.72) |
| Λητὼ δὲ προσέειπε διάκτορος ἀργεϊφόντης (21.497, whole line) | "And to Leto addressed the guide, Argeïphontes:" | "And the guide, the slayer of Argus, said to Leto:" | "the giant-killer", "the courier"; follows the table’s διάκτορος ἀργεϊφόντης |
| ἀργαλέον δὲ πληκτίζεσθ’ ἀλόχοισι Διὸς νεφεληγερέταο (21.498–499) | "for grievous it is to exchange blows with the wives of Zeus, the cloud-gatherer" | "for it is a grievous thing to exchange blows with the wives of Zeus who gathers the clouds" | "difficult", "wrestle", "brawl"; ἀργαλέος "grievous" (table), νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς as in the Odyssey table |
| ἀλλὰ μάλα πρόφρασσα μετ’ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν εὔχεσθαι ἐμὲ νικῆσαι (21.500–501) | "but, very ready-minded, among the immortal gods, declare yourself to have prevailed over me" | "but go ahead, with a ready mind, and declare among the immortal gods that you defeated me" | "boast", "gladly", "claim"; πρόφρασσα follows the table’s πρόφρων "ready-minded"; εὔχεσθαι "declare"; νικάω "prevailed over" / "defeated" as in the table (3.404) |
| κρατερῆφι βίηφιν (21.501) | "by strong might" | "by strong might" | "mighty force", "great strength" (reserved), "violence"; κρατερός "strong", βίη "might" as in the shipped ὑπὸ … βίηφιν (15.614) |
